summary: Added the operand the last interpretation named, and the draft-side run shows the provenance of the rejected change. Each rejection now carries log_types - the (index, EntryType) of the rejecting node's entries from its first index to its committed index - and for all three rejections at seed 35 it is '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2': a normal entry, a ConfChangeV2, a normal entry, then the rejected ConfChangeV2 at index 4. In EntryType terms the node consumed two joint-entering configuration entries with only a normal entry between them, i.e. no leave-joint entry before the second one - and a normal entry at index 3 is exactly what the target's propose-time rewrite produces when it drops a configuration change. Combined with the previous receipt's operands (applied_before=3 for nodes 3 and 1, 0 for the rebuilt node 4, reapplied_entry=false everywhere, batches starting at applied_before+1 or at the node's first entry), the picture is that the log itself carried a second joint-entering change behind an unapplied first one, which is the shape the propose-time guard is supposed to prevent by consulting the leader's own applied configuration and tracker. I deliberately did not assert the defect from a draft-side run: the submission requests isolated execution of these bytes so the log_types operands are receipt-backed first, and the request states the instrumentation (log_types capped at eight entries, alongside applied_before/applying_before/reapplied_entry and the entry and node operands), the assumption that log_types reports EntryType values only and not which change each ConfChangeV2 carries, and the limitation that the proposer's tracker and applied index at append time are still unobserved - which is what the next discriminator would need to show whether the guard's premise failed at the proposer or the proposer simply was not the node that saw the joint state.
